Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

same adjective

also the same, the same as, at the same time, one and the same, identical

classical

Cic. Off. 1.90: īdem semper vultus eademque frōns
Cic. Amic. 103: īdem vīctus

īdem, eadem, idem

pronoun

the same

“The same as” is īdem quī … or īdem atque (ac) …: idem velle atque idem nōlle, wanting and not wanting the same things (Sall. C. 20, Lewis & Short). Masculine īdem with a long i, neuter idem with a short one.

Other words

  • simul — at the same time, together

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. And. 3.2.31: multa concurrunt simul (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 2.12.1: ūnō tempore mihi datās duās

    Also ūnō tempore, at one and the same time.

  • īdem et pār — identical, the same and equal

    also used · classical · Traupman 331

  • identicus, identica, identicum — identical

    also used · modern · Traupman 331

    Not in Lewis & Short; a medieval and modern formation from idem.

Examples

  • ūna domus erat, īdem vīctus, isque commūnis

    there was one house, the same food, and that sharedCic. Amic. 103

  • praeclāraque est aequābilitās in omnī vītā et īdem semper vultus eademque frōns

    and a fine thing is evenness all through life, always the same face and the same browCic. Off. 1.90

  • quid est sapientia? semper idem velle atque idem nōlle

    what is wisdom? Always to want the same thing and refuse the same thingSen. Ep. 20.5

  • haec quae Pīcēnīs venit subducta trapētīs inchoat atque eadem fīnit olīva dapēs

    the olive that comes fresh from the presses of Picenum begins the meal, and the same olive ends itMart. 13.36.1–2

  • ūnus et īdem

    one and the sameTraupman 354

See also the same old song, it makes no difference, also.
